thermal perturbations which grow due to a radial variation in the viscous heating can be damped by the turbulence acting as a diffusion process.
the thermal perturbances are damped if the turbulent viscosity acts as diffusion, and are amplified if it does not.

the thermal stability of advection-dominated accretion flows against local thermal perturbances.

the thermal perturbances grow if the diffusion process is too weak, and the disks are geometricaly thin and the radiation pressure greatly dominates.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thermal perturbative instability of advection-dominated disks against local perturbation is weak and can be ignored.
thermal perturbations in advection-dominated disks are strongly damped if the diffusion process is strong enough.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the thermal instability in the inner regions of advection-dominated disks is strongly suppressed by turbulence.
thermal perturbations of advection-dominated disks against local perturbation are strongly damped by turbulence if it is treated as a diffusion process.
the stability of thermal perturbations in the advection-dominated disks is strongly dependent on the nature of the turbulent viscosity.
